messages:
maya: heads up — i'm planning a deploy for infra-service chart v3.4.0 into prod (01:00-02:00 UTC window). changes are resource tweaks and an env toggle. will run a `--dry-run` first. any concerns about enabling checksum/config annotation so helm forces pod restart on values change?

arun: can you paste the exact helm command and where the override file lives? also are we pinning chart deps?

maya: cmd i'm going to run for dry-run:```
helm upgrade infra-service chart/infra \
  --namespace infra-prod \
  --values ops/infra/overrides-prod.yaml \
  --set image.tag=release-2026-03 \
  --dry-run
```overrides-prod.yaml is in infra/ops repo (ops/infra/overrides-prod.yaml). chart dependencies are currently floating; i can pin the Chart.lock if we want.

deploy-bot: Pipeline queued: infra-service-deploy #789 — https://ci.internal/redwood/pipelines/789 :rocket: (dry-run step first)

kevin: LGTM for the dry-run. +1 for checksum annotation approach — we use `checksum/config` on the deployment to force rolling update when configmap/secret changes. example in our helm hooks:```yaml
metadata:
  annotations:
    checksum/config: "{{ include (sha256sum .Files.Get \"ops/infra/overrides-prod.yaml\") }}"
```

emily: please pin the chart dependency versions in Chart.lock and pin image tag (not :latest). if health checks fail we should rollback to previous revision and cut a hotfix branch. also add a short release note in the repo describing the change.

samuel: for rollback automation, recommend the following smoke test after deploy: send 50 reqs across 1m to /health and /search. if error rate > 10% or avg p95 latency increases > 300ms over baseline, trigger rollback. simple script:```bash
python tools/smoke_check.py --target infra-prod --checks 50 --max-error 0.1 --max-p95-delta 0.3
if [ $? -ne 0 ]; then helm rollback infra-service <REV>; fi
```

maya: @kevin can you be primary watcher for the window? i'll kick off the dry-run ~00:50 UTC and then promote if clean. :eyes:

kevin: yep i'll watch metrics and tracing. if we hit the threshold i'll run:```bash
helm rollback infra-service 42
kubectl -n infra-prod rollout status deploy/infra-service
```and ping @oncall-sre to coordinate DB/ingress fixes if needed. :thumbsup:

oncall-sre: if rollback occurs, also remember to clear any new autoscaler annotations and check that HPA target metrics are stable. if pods are not terminating, `kubectl delete pod --grace-period=0` as a last resort.

deploy-bot: Dry-run completed — no manifest errors. Proceed with real deploy? Approvals: @kevin, @emily.

emily: approved. go ahead after 00:55 UTC. i'll add a short release note and update Chart.lock after we confirm. :white_check_mark:
